clue.text: Befuddled by measure of strong drink, almost spotted the trumpeter

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter of that word is lost

parts.note: befuddled means giddy and confused
a gill is a small measure, traditionally used for spirits
espied means caught sight of

explanation.surface: Someone is fuddled after nearly a full measure of spirits, and thinks they caught sight of a trumpet player.
explanation.walkthrough: The trumpeter is a person, not a description: the famous American bebop jazzman with the bent horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy Gillespie was a celebrated American jazz musician famous for playing trumpet in bebop bands.

clue.text: Solved Plodge, suppressing quiet rage, but only half of Gemini?

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down inside, so one piece sits within the other
something solved has been worked out or dissolved, so the following word is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a made-up word supplying letters to rearrange
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
a plain synonym

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a fictional Inspector Plodge, solving a case while keeping a lid on fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Plodge rearranges to DOPELG, which takes P inside it; ANGER follows to make DOPPELGANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini are the heavenly twins, and one member of an identical pair resembles a ghostly double or lookalike.

clue.text: "Nul points" in the Brazil-Chile match

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words, running across the join

parts.note: the end of Brazil runs into the start of Chile

explanation.surface: A football match between Brazil and Chile ends with somebody scoring nothing, in Eurovision terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Nul points is the famous zero score announced in the Eurovision Song Contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Zilch is slang for nothing at all, the same as a score of zero points.

clue.text: County Kerry is getting Home Office worried

indicators.note: something worried is shaken about and disturbed, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the usual abbreviation for the UK government department

explanation.surface: A man named Kerry is fretting because the Home Office, the UK interior ministry, has taken an interest in him.
explanation.walkthrough: County Kerry is an Irish county, which tempts the solver to look in Ireland; the answer is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is a large historic county in the north of England.

clue.text: Child regarding what makes a painting stand out

definitions.text: what makes a painting stand out

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
as to means concerning

explanation.surface: A note about a child and whatever it is that makes a picture memorable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand out' looks figurative, meaning remarkable, but here it is literal: paint raised from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on thickly so that brushstrokes physically project from the canvas.

clue.text: Bird has triumph on stage with "Top Gun"

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the word for a win goes second

parts.note: a lap is one stage of a race
a plain synonym

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of gun

explanation.surface: A performer has a theatrical triumph with a stage version of the film Top Gun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, triumph placed on stage puts WIN beneath LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, or peewit, is a crested wading species of plover common on farmland.

clue.text: Swimmer concealing verse in crack

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish
v is the standard abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A swimmer hides a poem in a crevice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; in crosswords it is often a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or puzzle is to work out its answer.

clue.text: Native in charge after being canned without resistance

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for being in charge at the end
without is used in its old sense of outside, so the phrase wraps around the other piece

parts.note: canned goods are in tins
R is the physics symbol for resistance
the standard abbreviation, as in 2ic

explanation.surface: A local is put in charge after being sacked, without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like slang for dismissed, which fits 'in charge', but it means put in tins.
explanation.definitionFit: Native qualities are inborn ones, belonging to the essential nature of something.

clue.text: River god adopting extreme position

definitions.note: describes the stance, as an adjective would

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A river god takes up a radical stance.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar views lie at opposite ends of a range, as far apart from each other as possible.

clue.text: Supply inhabitants with two drugs, digesting the Letters of Paul …

indicators.note: digesting means taking something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: pot is cannabis and E is ecstasy

indicators.note: taking just the letters of a name lets them be set out in any order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stocks a place with residents while drugged up and reading St Paul's Epistles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Letters of Paul are the Epistles, which the ellipsis carries into 11 across; here only the four letters of the name are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To populate a place is to fill it with people who live there.

clue.text: Surprise attack on aristocrat in pub (The Grove)

indicators.note: in places the nobleman inside the abbreviation for a pub

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
an earl is a nobleman
an arbour is a shady bower of trees

explanation.surface: A nobleman is set upon in a pub called The Grove.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grove reads as a pub's name, but it is a separate piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese raid on the US Pacific fleet in December 1941 came without warning and brought America into the war.

clue.text: … where one was sent to the lost sheep of America

indicators.note: lost animals have wandered astray, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A biblical mission to the lost sheep, reworked to send them to America.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 9 across: 'one' is one of Paul's letters, the Epistle to the Ephesians. 'The lost sheep' recalls Jesus' mission to the lost sheep of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul addressed an epistle to the church at Ephesus, an ancient city in Asia Minor.

clue.text: Break down and put it to death, beheaded

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its head, its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
demise is a formal word for death

explanation.surface: Something collapses and is executed by decapitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put it to death, beheaded' reads as one grim instruction, but beheaded applies only to the word for death.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down a bill or total is to list its separate parts one by one.

clue.text: Twins dropping note to one or more spirits

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so the musical syllable is taken out

parts.note: Gemini is the zodiac sign of the Twins
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Twins lose a note and are compared to a ghost or two.
explanation.walkthrough: One does double duty: it gives the final letter and opens the definition, since the word has been used as both singular and plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii, plural of genie or genius, are supernatural beings such as guardian spirits or the jinn of Arabian tales.

clue.text: Girl hides the way to 3's location

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the girl's name wraps the next word

parts.note: a girl's name
taken as written
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A girl conceals the route to somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to the answer at 3 down, YORKSHIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire lies in the north-eastern part of England, one compass direction from the centre.

clue.text: Yellow aromatic plant received by former monarch's co-ordinator

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

indicators.note: being received by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, stands for a past King George
anise is a herb with liquorice-scented seeds

explanation.surface: A cowardly co-ordinator of an old king grows a fragrant herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow here is not cowardice but the heraldic colour, followed by the herb inside the king's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: An organiser arranges events and brings people together, which is what a co-ordinator does.

clue.text: Forged metal pane or plaque with handle

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between a wrought-metal panel and a plaque with a grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Handle means a name here, as in a nickname, not a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a small plaque bearing someone's name, and a handle is slang for a name.

clue.text: Ladies one interrupted hurry back to the childminder

indicators.note: back tells us the whole string is read the other way round
something interrupted has another item breaking into its middle

parts.note: dames are ladies
the Roman numeral for one
to run is to hurry

explanation.surface: Women interrupted by someone hurry back to the person looking after their children.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, a domestic childminder.

clue.text: State taking wing by degrees

parts.note: ala is the anatomical Latin term for a wing
BA and MA are university degrees

explanation.surface: A government department acquires a new wing, little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' looks like the idiom for gradually; here it means academic degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Challenged about compiler being greatly elevated

indicators.note: about means round, so the word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to defy is to challenge
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter is defied about being exalted.
explanation.walkthrough: Compiler is the setter, who writes as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deified is to be made into a god, raised to the very highest status.

clue.text: He prophesied the Cockney Creator

indicators.note: Cockney signals the next word as said in a London East End accent

parts.note: a Cockney pronounces maker with an 'eye' vowel and dropped final R

explanation.surface: A prophet foretold the coming of a London-accented God.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of London's East End, where the 'ay' vowel sounds like 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Chained runaway insectivore

indicators.note: a runaway has broken loose, so the letters escape their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tethered animal that eats insects has escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying Australian mammal feeding on ants and termites.

clue.text: Opened and closed without a winner

definitions.meaning: curtains that are pulled can be either pulled open or pulled shut
a game that ends level has no victor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened and closed' sounds like a contradiction; one word for curtains covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains are pulled either open or shut, and a level match ends with neither side victorious.

clue.text: Shed isn't as bright as Vlad

parts.note: Shed is the setter, who says I'm of himself
less bright means paler

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being dimmer than a notorious prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Shed isn't as bright' is the setter saying I'M PALER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlad III of Wallachia, the inspiration for Dracula, was nicknamed for impaling his enemies on stakes.

clue.text: It shoots down toboggan runs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a German semi-automatic pistol
second meaning: someone who rides a small racing sled feet first

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about something speeding downhill; split it after 'shoots'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a famous German pistol and also a competitor who races a small sled on an ice track.

clue.text: Desert, boundless desert, devoured by devouring goddess

indicators.note: being devoured means being swallowed up inside something
without bounds means losing both its edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: the great desert of North Africa
Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction, often shown devouring

explanation.surface: One desert is swallowed whole by a greedy goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kalahari is a large semi-arid sandy region of southern Africa, covering much of Botswana.

clue.text: Ructions as head gilder separates silver from gold backing

indicators.note: something that separates two items sits between them

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of gilder

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so that word is read in reverse

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in a workshop when the chief gilder sorts silver from gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ructions are noisy rows and disturbances, the same kind of trouble the slang word describes.

clue.text: The average porter is a model of excellence

parts.note: standard means ordinary or normal
a porter carries things, as a bearer does

explanation.surface: An ordinary porter turns out to be exemplary.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'average' and 'excellence' contradict each other, yet both describe the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer is a leading figure who upholds a cause and sets an example for others.
